liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Truckin'** (3 reviews): The sequence from Space through Truckin' into Stella Blue is singled out as the show's highlight; The short but rocking Truckin' into Stella Blue is called the show's star [14][19][21]
- **Mexicali Blues** (2 reviews): Reviewer praises the Mama Tried segue into Mexicali Blues; Bob's singing makes this normally unremarkable tune stand out [14][19]
- **Promised Land** (1 review): Reviewer calls it very hot [15]
- **Friend of the Devil** (1 review): Played in a soft, gentle way [13]
- **Lazy Lightning** (1 review): The Lazy Lightning into Supplication pairing is called especially hot [15]
- **Saint of Circumstance** (1 review): The song reaches an ending the reviewer finds perfect [14]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): Reviewer calls it top notch [22]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): The closing solo is described as beautifully hypnotic [21]

## The recordings

- **gd80-05-08.sbd.carman.15034.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 146 min; rated 4.41/5 by 17 [1]. Said about its sound: Clear and well mixed soundboard; Crisp soundboard with levels that are nearly perfect; The tape sounds nice [12][19][22]
- **gd1980-05-08.152804.senn.blend.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 152 min [3]
- **gd1980-05-08.fob.sonyecm999.morris.100243.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 147 min; rated 3.75/5 by 4 [6]. Said about its sound: There is a tape flip between drums and space [6]
- **gd1980-05-08.nak700.wise.miller.100401.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 150 min; rated 3.5/5 by 4 [7]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says they attended every show on this tour [20]
- Reviewer ranks its sound among the best of 1980, apart from a few October shows [12]
- Reviewer suggests the last night at Nassau, a week or so later, was similarly hot [15]
- Eight months earlier, the same venue's show was this reviewer's low point; this one ranked among the highs [17]
- Reviewer rates it a top-five show out of 200+, behind the Cape Cod shows and 12/31/81 [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd80-05-08.sbd.carman.15034.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Primary source is a master soundboard cassette, copied to cassette, then DAT, then CDR; Patched with Jim Wise's audience recording, received via Jeff Hellman, made with two Nak 700s and a Nak 300; patched by R. Carman [1]
- **gd1980-05-08.152804.senn.blend.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Recorded, Transferred and Mastered by Rob Eaton; transferred by Mastered by Scott Clugston April 2021; source: Rob Eaton's Master Audience Cassettes; (2)Sennheiser 441 mics (Left + Right) + (1) Sennheiser 421 mic (Center) blend > Nakamichi 550 [3]. Also: Master recording and transfer come from Rob Eaton, with Charlie Miller coordinating the release; A Nakamichi 700 and 300 blend source supplies short patches in Bertha and Drums [3]
- **gd1980-05-08.fob.sonyecm999.morris.100243.flac16**: taped by Bob Morris; source: (FOB) Sony ECM-990 stereo mic > Cassette Master (Marantz Superscope CD320 Maxell UDXLI); Recorded from Section 103, Row P, Seat 14 [6]
- **gd1980-05-08.nak700.wise.miller.100401.flac16**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (3) Nakamichi CM700 Shotguns -> Namakmichi 550 -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Maxell UDXLII-C90/Dolby B) [7]. Also: Jim Wise lent his master cassettes; Joe B. Jones helped with pitch correction [7]
